concepts.name: India–Pakistan Border: Radcliffe Line and Its Contested Segments
key_dimensions: Origin and demarcation of the Radcliffe Line (1947) and its legal status
Distinction between the International Border (IB), Line of Control (LoC), and Actual Ground Position Line (AGPL) in J&K
Sir Creek dispute: thalweg principle vs. fixed boundary claim, implications for maritime zones
Siachen Glacier: location of AGPL, strategic peaks (Saltoro Ridge), and why it is the world's highest battlefield

concepts.name: India–China Border: McMahon Line and Line of Actual Control (LAC)
key_dimensions: McMahon Line origin (Simla Convention 1914) — China's non-acceptance vs. India's acceptance
Three-sector division of LAC: Western (Ladakh), Middle (Himachal/Uttarakhand), Eastern (Arunachal/Sikkim)
Key friction points: Aksai Chin (under Chinese control, claimed by India), Depsang Plains, Galwan Valley, Doklam
UPSC trap: LAC ≠ McMahon Line; McMahon Line applies only to the Eastern sector

concepts.name: India–China Border: Aksai Chin and Arunachal Pradesh Disputes
key_dimensions: Aksai Chin: administered by China, claimed by India as part of Ladakh (UT); strategic highway NH-219
Arunachal Pradesh: India's 'rising sun state' vs. China's claim as 'South Tibet' (Zangnan)
Tawang Monastery: geo-cultural flashpoint; its location relative to McMahon Line
UPSC trap: Aksai Chin is in the Western sector; Arunachal dispute is in the Eastern sector — do not conflate

concepts.name: India–Bangladesh Border: Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) 2015
key_dimensions: Enclaves (Chitmahals): concept of counter-enclaves and counter-counter-enclaves; Dahagram–Angarpota corridor
Teen Bigha Corridor: India's lease to Bangladesh, purpose, and its connectivity function
LBA 2015: constitutional amendment required (100th Amendment Act), exchange of enclaves
Rivers forming the border: Padma (Ganges), Brahmaputra, Meghna; Farakka Barrage upstream tensions

concepts.name: India–Nepal Border: Open Border and Disputed Territories
key_dimensions: Sugauli Treaty (1816): historical basis of the India–Nepal boundary
Kalapani–Lipulekh–Limpiyadhura dispute: India's claim vs. Nepal's 2020 revised map
Open border policy: implications for movement of people, goods, and security concerns
UPSC trap: Susta area (West Champaran, Bihar) is another disputed segment — less commonly known

concepts.name: India–Bhutan Border and Special Relationship
key_dimensions: Friendship Treaty (2007): replaced 1949 treaty; Bhutan conducts foreign policy independently but coordinates with India
Doklam Plateau: tri-junction of India–China–Bhutan; 2017 standoff — why India intervened on behalf of Bhutan
Bhutan–China border negotiations: areas Bhutan is negotiating (Pasamlung, Jakarlung) could affect India's Siliguri Corridor
UPSC trap: Bhutan is the only neighbour that does NOT share any maritime boundary with India

concepts.name: India–Myanmar Border: Free Movement Regime and Strategic Features
key_dimensions: Free Movement Regime (FMR): 16 km zone on both sides; India's decision to review/fence the border (2023)
States sharing border with Myanmar: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram (mnemonic: ANMM)
Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project: route significance for India's Act East Policy
UPSC trap: Myanmar shares border with 4 Indian states — not 3; Arunachal is often missed

concepts.name: India–Sri Lanka Maritime Boundary: Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar
key_dimensions: Katchatheevu Island: ceded to Sri Lanka via 1974 agreement; fishermen's rights controversy
Palk Strait vs. Palk Bay vs. Gulf of Mannar: precise geographic distinctions
Adam's Bridge (Ram Setu): chain of limestone shoals; Sethusamudram Canal Project controversy
UPSC trap: India has NO land boundary with Sri Lanka; the separation is the Palk Strait (~65 km wide)

concepts.name: India–Maldives Maritime Relations and EEZ Overlap
key_dimensions: Minicoy Island (India) and Maldives: proximity and EEZ delimitation issues
India's strategic concern: 'India First' policy of Maldives and Chinese presence in the Indian Ocean
Hydrographic surveys and maritime security agreements with India
UPSC trap: India has NO land boundary with Maldives; closest Indian territory is Minicoy (Lakshadweep)

concepts.name: Siliguri Corridor (Chicken's Neck): Strategic Vulnerability
key_dimensions: Geography: ~22 km wide strip in West Bengal connecting Northeast India to the mainland
Countries surrounding the corridor: Nepal (N/NW), Bangladesh (S), Bhutan (N), China (via Bhutan in the North)
Strategic importance: only land route to 7 Northeastern states; vulnerability in conflict scenarios
UPSC trap: The corridor is NOT bordered directly by China — it is bordered by Bhutan, which itself borders China

concepts.name: Tri-Junction Points Among India and Its Neighbours
key_dimensions: India–China–Nepal tri-junction: Lipulekh Pass area (currently disputed)
India–China–Bhutan tri-junction: Doklam/Batangla area (strategic flashpoint)
India–Bangladesh–Myanmar tri-junction: near Feni River/Cox's Bazar area
UPSC trap: India has no tri-junction with Pakistan and Afghanistan — Afghanistan and Pakistan share a tri-junction with China (Wakhan Corridor) but India is not involved

concepts.name: India–Pakistan: Sir Creek and Maritime Boundary Dispute
key_dimensions: Location: Sir Creek is a 96 km estuary in the Rann of Kutch, separating Gujarat (India) from Sindh (Pakistan)
Core dispute: India claims boundary runs along the eastern bank; Pakistan claims it runs along the middle (thalweg)
Impact on EEZ and continental shelf: resolution could shift maritime boundary significantly
UPSC trap: Sir Creek is in the Arabian Sea (west coast), not in the Bay of Bengal; often confused with eastern coastal disputes

concepts.name: India's Land Borders: State-wise Distribution and Length
key_dimensions: Longest land border: Bangladesh (~4,156 km); shortest: Afghanistan (~106 km, now effectively non-functional post-PoK)
States sharing maximum international boundaries: West Bengal (borders 3 countries: Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan)
States/UTs that share borders with Pakistan: J&K, Ladakh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat
UPSC trap: Sikkim shares border with China AND Nepal AND Bhutan but NOT with Bangladesh — a common mix-up

concepts.name: India–Afghanistan Border: Durand Line Context and Current Status
key_dimensions: Historical context: Durand Line (1893) separates Afghanistan from Pakistan (not India directly)
India's boundary with Afghanistan existed through the princely state of Jammu & Kashmir (Trans-Karakoram Tract area)
Post-1947: The border is now under Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir (PoAK/Gilgit-Baltistan), making it inaccessible to India
UPSC trap: India claims it has a boundary with Afghanistan through J&K — this is India's official position, though physically inaccessible

concepts.name: High Passes on India's Northern and Northwestern Borders
key_dimensions: India–China passes: Nathu La (Sikkim — reopened 2006 for trade), Jelep La (Sikkim), Bomdi La (Arunachal), Lipulekh (Uttarakhand)
India–Pakistan/PoK: Zoji La (J&K — connects Srinagar to Leh), Khardung La (Ladakh — among world's highest motorable passes)
Strategic vs. trade passes: which are open for bilateral trade vs. restricted military zones
UPSC trap: Nathu La connects India to Tibet (China), NOT to Nepal; Lipulekh connects to Tibet but is disputed with Nepal

concepts.name: Rivers as International Boundaries Between India and Neighbours
key_dimensions: India–Bangladesh: Padma, Meghna, Brahmaputra, Feni, Teesta (Teesta water-sharing dispute)
India–Pakistan: Ravi, Beas, Sutlej (Indus Waters Treaty 1960 allocation), Chenab, Jhelum
India–Nepal: Gandak, Kosi, Mahakali (Sarada) — each has a separate treaty/agreement
UPSC trap: The Indus itself does NOT form the India–Pakistan boundary; it flows through Pakistan after entering from Ladakh

concepts.name: India's Coastal/Maritime Neighbours vs. Land Neighbours
key_dimensions: Land neighbours (7): Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Afghanistan (claimed)
Maritime neighbours: Sri Lanka, Maldives, Indonesia (maritime boundary in Andaman Sea), Thailand (maritime), Myanmar (also land)
Countries sharing ONLY maritime boundary with India: Sri Lanka, Maldives, Indonesia
UPSC trap: Indonesia shares a maritime boundary with India (near Andaman & Nicobar Islands) — often overlooked in favour of only listing SAARC neighbours

concepts.name: Zero Line, Boundary Pillars, and Demarcation Mechanisms
key_dimensions: Joint boundary commissions: India–Bangladesh Joint Boundary Working Group; India–Pakistan boundary pillar maintenance
Distinction: Demarcated (physically marked), Delimited (on paper/map), Undemarcated boundaries
India–China LAC: not demarcated or delimited — both sides have different perceptions of where it runs
UPSC trap: The LoC with Pakistan is demarcated (following Simla Agreement 1972); the LAC with China is NOT demarcated — a critical legal/strategic difference

concepts.name: Rann of Kutch: Geographical and Boundary Significance
key_dimensions: Great Rann vs. Little Rann: location, seasonal inundation, and ecological profile (flamingo breeding ground)
India–Pakistan boundary in Rann of Kutch: decided by International Tribunal (1968) — awarded 90% to India, 10% to Pakistan
Strategic significance: proximity to Sir Creek dispute area; BSF deployment challenges in marshy terrain
UPSC trap: The Rann of Kutch Award (1968) is one of the few India–Pakistan boundary disputes settled through international arbitration — most others remain unresolved

concepts.name: Northeast India's Boundary Complexity: China, Myanmar, and Bangladesh
key_dimensions: Arunachal Pradesh borders: China (north/northeast), Bhutan (west), Myanmar (east) — 3 international boundaries
Meghalaya–Bangladesh border: Meghalaya disputes 12 areas with Bangladesh (resolved partially in 2021 MoU)
Mizoram–Myanmar border: ethnic Chin–Mizo kinship; refugee influx post-2021 Myanmar coup
UPSC trap: Tripura is surrounded on three sides by Bangladesh — it is NOT landlocked because it has a border with Mizoram, but is often called 'almost an enclave'
